subject.title: Group chat sessions not persisted — only 1 session from 166+ messages

question: Should the remaining fix be owned by Telegram plain-group last-route construction, by a shared non-direct session fallback, or by another session-store durability path after live proof?
rationale: The source-supported symptom crosses Telegram routing and shared session persistence, and the only direct all-groups fix was closed while the shared fallback PR remains open and unproven for this issue.

options.title: Require live proof then choose one canonical fix
options.body: Run a redacted current-main Telegram plain-group restart proof, then sponsor either the Telegram-specific or shared fallback fix based on the observed failing path.

options.title: Repair the shared fallback PR
options.body: Refresh or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77442 only if maintainers want missing updateLastRoute handling solved generically for all non-direct channels.

options.title: Limit this to Telegram groups
options.body: Reopen or recreate the narrow all-groups Telegram updateLastRoute fix if maintainers decide the shared fallback is too broad for this issue.

recommendation.title: Require live proof then choose one canonical fix
recommendation.body: Run a redacted current-main Telegram plain-group restart proof, then sponsor either the Telegram-specific or shared fallback fix based on the observed failing path.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily about the shared inbound session recorder versus channel-owned last-route behavior, and steipete has the clearest history on that shared path.
